I have an important announcement today. Recently, our school has
installed vending machines in the dormitory. But many students have
complained that the items in the vending machines do not fully meet
their tastes. To address this, we are conducting an online survey to
gather your suggestions on what products you’d like to see in the
vending machines. The survey link will be sent to you in a text
message after this announcement. Please take a few minutes to
answer the survey by this Friday. Your opinion is important, and
we’re looking forward to receiving your ideas. Thank you!

questions.script:
W: Mr. Johnson, we’re almost done with the major decisions about the
interior design of your house. Now you just need to choose the
color for your living room wall paper.
M: That’s right. I’ve seen the color samples you’ve sent, but I can’t
decide which one to choose. Do you have any advice?
W: Well, there’s one important thing you need to consider when you
choose a wall color.
M: One important thing? What is it?
W: If you go with light colors, they will make the space look larger and
more open.
M: Interesting. So, dark colors make a space appear smaller?
W: Exactly. This is because light colors reflect natural light and make a
space appear larger to the eyes.
M: Hmm... Since my living room is a bit small, I’ll go with white.
W: That’s a great choice! It’s always important to consider the size of
the space when choosing a wall paper color. A light color like white
will definitely create a sense of openness in your living room.
M: Thank you for helping me.

M: Hello, everyone. Today, I am going to talk about how we can
support senior citizens in the digital age. You may have heard that
many seniors are struggling with digital technologies in their daily
lives, such as ordering food at kiosks or using mobile banking apps.
Because they are not familiar with these digital services, seniors
may find it difficult to keep up with all the changes in today’s
world. That’s why we need to provide them with digital education.
By teaching seniors how to utilize digital skills, we can help them
navigate modern life smoothly and they won’t feel left behind.

M: Ms. Anderson, are we all set for the culture exchange program with
the French students?
W: It’s going well, Mr. Grant. Do you want to go over what we’ve done
so far?
M: Sure. I’ve been teaching our students some basic French greetings,
and they’ve been practicing their welcome speech.
W: That sounds nice. Your efforts will definitely help the exchange
students feel welcome. I’ve prepared all the traditional craft
materials for them.
M: It would be great if the students could work in pairs for the
traditional crafts session.
W: Exactly. I’ve already made a list of pairs. I paired one student from

M: Good. And I’ve ordered keyrings to use as souvenirs. They should
arrive this afternoon.

arrive? I think I won’t have time for that.

questions.script:
W: Welcome to Gardener’s! How can I help you?
M: Hi! I’d like to add some new flowers to my garden.
W: That’s wonderful! What flowers do you have in mind?
M: I like lilies. How much are they?
W: They’re $4 each.
M: I’ll take five lilies. Can you recommend any other flowers? I was
thinking of mixing a few different types.
W: In that case, how about pairing them with some tulips?
M: Oh, that sounds great. How much are the tulips?
W: They’re half the price of lilies — just $2 each.
M: Great. I’ll take five tulips, then.
W: Five lilies and five tulips, right? When you buy 10 flowers or more,
we offer a 10% discount.
M: Thank you. Here’s my credit card.

questions.script:
M: Hey, Betty. Did you get the result of the class photo contest?
W: Unfortunately, my class couldn’t even take part in the contest.
M: No way! What happened? Your classmates love taking photos.
W: Yeah, we often take pictures together.
M: Then you could have submitted one of your existing photos. Was
there any unexpected problem like the size requirement of the
photo?
W: No, the size met the requirements. And we were okay with the fact
that we should submit a photo taken outdoors.
M: Hmm... Then what was the problem? You didn’t accidentally delete
the photo for the contest, did you?
W: No. The truth is I thought the deadline was 17th but it was 12th.
M: Oh, no. I’m sorry to hear that. But don’t beat yourself up about it
too much. Everyone makes mistakes sometimes.
W: Thanks. But I still feel so bad about it.

up soon.
W: That sounds great! I’ve competed in several swimming events, but
never anything like this. Are you going to participate?
M: Absolutely. I’ve been training for both swimming and running.
W: When is the event?
M: It’s on May 24th.
W: I’d like to join, too. Have you completed the registration process?
M: Not yet. I heard we need to register online by filling out a form.
Let’s sign up together.
W: Sounds good. How about training together before the event?
M: Great idea. The competition will be held at Blue River. Why don’t
we find a similar place to practice?
W: I know the best place. Let’s get started this weekend!

W: Hello, listeners. I’m Hannah Carter from the Sunnyville Pet Fair
organizing committee. I’m excited to announce that this year’s pet
fair will take place on Saturday, April 19th, at the Sunnyville
Community Park. During the event, there will be a dog training
program by Mike Harris, a well­known pet behavior expert. We will
also host a pet costume contest, where pets can show off their best

cost $5 per person, and all the profits will be donated to local

this exciting event!

W: Hello, students. Have any of you visited a museum recently? If so,
you may have noticed some remarkable changes taking place.
Today, I’d like to share some insights about the changes happening
in museums. Now, traditional museums are being transformed by
modern technologies. The first technology I want to introduce is
virtual reality. Museums around the world are adopting virtual
reality to change how visitors interact with historical objects. For
instance, visitors can now explore ancient buildings as if they were
real. Another technology being used in museums is 3D animation.
This brings historical scenes to life, showing how people lived in
the past. Animated displays allow visitors to experience historical
events in a more engaging way. Also, laser projection creates
dynamic effects on gallery walls. Using this technology, museums
can highlight specific artworks and create fascinating environments
that enhance the viewing experience. Finally, 3D printing has
opened up new possibilities for museums. This technology makes it
possible to display accurate copies of delicate or rare items that
cannot be exposed to the public. These technological innovations are
making museum collections more accessible, interactive, and
engaging than ever before.
